logicalBugs.description: A Gitea repository with exactly one Git tag, a named code revision, displays “1 Tags” in the Tags page heading. The nearby tab correctly says “1 Tag,” making the inconsistent pluralization visible on the same page.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The tags template renders a numeric count beside the fixed repo.release.tags label rather than a count-aware translation.
reproductionPaths: A Gitea repository with exactly one Git tag, a named code revision, displays “1 Tags” in the Tags page heading. The nearby tab correctly says “1 Tag,” making the inconsistent pluralization visible on the same page.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s repository Releases RSS feed includes a link back to its release listing. That generated link uses /release/ instead of the working /releases route, so following the feed’s channel link opens Page Not Found even though the release list exists.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ShowReleaseFeed constructs /release instead of the /releases route.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s repository Releases RSS feed includes a link back to its release listing. That generated link uses /release/ instead of the working /releases route, so following the feed’s channel link opens Page Not Found even though the release list exists.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a published release appears as an item in the repository’s activity RSS feed. Its generated link incorrectly includes refs/tags/ as part of the tag destination and opens Page Not Found instead of the release details.
logicalBugs.rootCause: toReleaseLink appends act.GetBranch(), which for tag creation contains refs/tags, rather than the normalized tag name.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, a published release appears as an item in the repository’s activity RSS feed. Its generated link incorrectly includes refs/tags/ as part of the tag destination and opens Page Not Found instead of the release details.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, New Release accepts tag names that later fail Git creation, including a 251–255-character filename component or a parent/child ref namespace conflict. Submit replaces the editor with HTTP 500 and a raw Git/filesystem error instead of keeping a recoverable tag-name error in the form.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The release form accepts Git-ref names and length up to 255, while createTag reports only selected invalid-name errors; valid names exceeding filesystem component limits or conflicting with existing ref directories escape as server failures.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s new-release form permits a 255-character tag name, but submitting a 251–255-character ASCII tag replaces the editor with a filename-too-long server error.
In Gitea, creating a tag whose name conflicts with an existing parent or child tag namespace replaces the release editor with a raw Git error page.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, below 439px, New/Edit Release controls stretch to the full field width even when they are checkboxes or toolbar buttons. Pre-Release and tag-message checkboxes overlap their labels, checked/unchecked task boxes in Preview become indistinguishable bars, and the legacy editor toolbar can become a tall single-button column.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The max-width 438px CSS applies width:100% to every .field input/button, including native checkbox controls, preview task-list checkboxes and legacy toolbar buttons.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, at 390×844 CSS pixels, the New Release form stretches the Pre-Release checkbox input across its label, placing the native checkbox glyph over the text.

In Gitea, below 439px wide, the New Release form stretches the “Use the title and content of release as tag message” checkbox to the full field width, so its check glyph sits in the middle of the label text.
In Gitea, below 439px wide, task-list checkboxes in the New/Edit Release notes Preview are stretched to the full field width with no check mark, so checked and unchecked tasks look the same.

In Gitea, at phone widths, switching the release notes to the legacy editor lays out each toolbar button on its own full-width row, so the toolbar stretches roughly a screen tall before the notes field.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a Git tag can mark a code revision without having a published release or release notes. For such a tag, the Tags list correctly offers New Release, but the tag’s detail page says the user “released this,” incorrectly describing a tag-only object as a release.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared release list template renders repo.released_this without branching on IsTag.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s Tags page, open a Git tag that has no published release. Although the list offers New Release for that tag, the detail page describes the tagging user as having “released this,” incorrectly presenting tag creation as release publication.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a release is a published description of a named code version, and its status badge identifies a Pre-Release or an unpublished Draft. Beside long or wrapping titles at constrained widths, these badges shrink and clip: Pre-Release loses its final characters on phones on either the Releases list or the individual release details page, and Draft can become “Dra” at tablet width. The saved release state itself is unchanged.
logicalBugs.rootCause: release-list-title is a flex row whose badge has no nonshrinking sizing; constrained mobile/tablet title rows compress the badge text.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, a newly published Pre-Release displays a clipped “Pre-Relea” badge in the mobile Releases listing, and the clipping remains after refresh.
In Gitea, at 768 CSS pixels, saving a draft with a wrapping title leaves its yellow status badge clipped to “Dra” at the card's right edge.

In Gitea, publish a Pre-Release with a long readable title, then open its individual details page at /releases/tag/<tag> on a 390-pixel-wide phone viewport. When the title wraps, the orange Pre-Release badge beside it is cut down to text such as “Pre-Re”. A short title at that width, or the same long title at desktop width, displays the full badge.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, operations > Create tag on a commit creates a valid, browsable Git tag, a name for that code revision. Choosing New Release for it recognizes the existing tag but Publish Release fails with “Target branch does not exist,” and no target selector is available to repair it. Tags created through the separate Create Tag Only flow can be converted to releases successfully.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CreateNewTag stores the supplied commit SHA in Release.Target, while NewReleasePost requires Target to be an existing branch even when converting an existing tag.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, operations > Create tag on a commit creates a valid, browsable Git tag, a name for that code revision. Choosing New Release for it recognizes the existing tag but Publish Release fails with “Target branch does not exist,” and no target selector is available to repair it. Tags created through the separate Create Tag Only flow can be converted to releases successfully.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a branch, which tracks ongoing code development, and a tag, which names a code revision, can share a name while pointing to different commits. When publishing a release with that branch explicitly selected as its target, the new release tag is created at the existing same-named tag’s commit instead of the selected branch’s commit.
logicalBugs.rootCause: createTag calls GetCommit(rel.Target) using the bare branch name instead of refs/heads, allowing a same-named tag to take precedence.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, create a branch and a tag with the same name but different target commits. In New Release, explicitly choose that branch as the target and publish a new release tag; the new tag points to the existing same-named tag’s commit instead of the chosen branch.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a tag’s detail page shows how many commits it is behind the repository’s default branch. If the tag points to a branch with a longer history, this counter can become negative instead of describing a meaningful relationship between the two histories.
logicalBugs.rootCause: calReleaseNumCommitsBehind subtracts release.NumCommits from the target history count; divergent or longer tag histories can yield negative numbers.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, create a tag on a branch whose history contains more commits than the default branch. Its tag details show a negative “commits behind” count instead of a meaningful comparison with the default branch.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on a commit page, repeating Operations > Create tag with an existing tag name correctly refuses the duplicate. The error nevertheless says a branch is being created, misidentifying the tag operation; no duplicate-tag creation is claimed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared NewBranchPost duplicate handling flashes repo.branch.branch_already_exists for CreateTag as well as branch creation.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on a commit page, repeating Operations > Create tag with an existing tag name correctly refuses the duplicate. The error nevertheless says a branch is being created, misidentifying the tag operation; no duplicate-tag creation is claimed.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a Git tag names a particular code revision and appears in the repository’s Tags list. At phone width, a tag without a published release can hide part of New Release and all of Delete Tag beyond the visible row without a usable horizontal-scroll route. A tag with a published release can instead clip its Release details link while the visible part remains usable. The same widened tag layout can also center a Delete Release confirmation offscreen and clip its warning or Yes button.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The tag list keeps its row metadata and actions on a constrained nonwrapping row; the row minimum geometry widens the document, also miscentering delete dialogs.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, at a 390×844 viewport, the tag row clips New Release and leaves Delete Tag outside the visible row; ordinary horizontal scrolling on the row and page does not expose the actions.

In Gitea, on a phone-width screen, the Delete Release confirmation dialog extends past the right edge of the viewport, cutting off its warning text and part of the Yes button, and it can't be scrolled into view. The release page's tag row has a minimum width that makes the page wider than the screen, and the dialog centres on that wider page.

In Gitea, publish a release on a new tag, then open the repository’s Tags page at a 390-pixel-wide phone viewport and find that tag. Its Release details action is clipped to text such as “Release de” at the right edge, although tapping the visible portion still opens the release. At 414 pixels and wider the full action text is visible. This is the published-release row variant of the clipped tag actions.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on New Release, upload an attachment successfully and then submit a form with another invalid field. The validation response keeps the other release values but drops the completed upload. Correcting the invalid field and saving creates the release or draft without the attachment unless the user uploads it again.
logicalBugs.rootCause: NewReleasePost re-renders on validation error without reconstructing attachment rows from form.Files, so already uploaded UUIDs are omitted on resubmission.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on New Release, upload an attachment successfully and then submit a form with another invalid field. The validation response keeps the other release values but drops the completed upload. Correcting the invalid field and saving creates the release or draft without the attachment unless the user uploads it again.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, release notes can contain nested Markdown lists. The same saved text displays different nested bullet styles in New Release Preview and on the published release, so the preview does not accurately show the final list presentation.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The published release wraps notes in render-content markup, while the editor preview uses a different rendering/styling container, so nested lists inherit different marker rules.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, release notes can contain nested Markdown lists. The same saved text displays different nested bullet styles in New Release Preview and on the published release, so the preview does not accurately show the final list presentation.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, at phone width, the New Release form’s Tag name field remains wider than the viewport while the title and notes fields fit. Entering or reviewing the tag therefore requires dealing with a field that extends offscreen instead of a form sized to the device.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The .target rule sets min-width:500px without a phone override.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, at phone width, the New Release form’s Tag name field remains wider than the viewport while the title and notes fields fit. Entering or reviewing the tag therefore requires dealing with a field that extends offscreen instead of a form sized to the device.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, Git tag names are case-sensitive, so two names differing only in capitalization can identify different revisions. After a lowercase release exists, both Publish Release and Create Tag Only reject an otherwise valid differently capitalized tag name as a duplicate instead of treating it as distinct.
logicalBugs.rootCause: IsReleaseExist and GetRelease look up LowerTagName using strings.ToLower, treating distinct case-only Git tag names as one record.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, Git tag names are case-sensitive, so two names differing only in capitalization can identify different revisions. After a lowercase release exists, both Publish Release and Create Tag Only reject an otherwise valid differently capitalized tag name as a duplicate instead of treating it as distinct.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, submitting an existing release edit with an empty required title redraws saved values over pending notes/pre-release changes. For a draft, the same error also loses attachment changes and draft controls; correcting the title can leave only Update Release and publish a draft the user intended to keep unpublished.
logicalBugs.rootCause: EditReleasePost populates title/content/prerelease from the saved release before HasError and omits IsDraft, attachments and attachment-enabled metadata supplied by GET. Error re-render therefore resets edits, hides uploads, and changes draft buttons into Update Release.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, submitting an existing release edit with an empty required title shows validation feedback but replaces the submitted notes and checked prerelease state with the saved values.

In Gitea, editing a draft release and clicking Save Draft with an empty title shows a validation error, but the re-rendered form loses the draft's Save Draft and Publish buttons and offers only Update Release. Clicking it after fixing the title publishes the release and creates its tag, although the user only meant to save a draft.

In Gitea, editing a draft release, renaming or removing an attachment, and clicking Save Draft with an empty title shows the title error, but the re-rendered form has no attachment rows or upload area, so the pending attachment renames and removals are lost.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, source archive downloads can contain a different commit from the branch/tag being viewed when its short name is ambiguous. A branch sharing a name with a tag can download the tag’s tree, and a tag named as another commit’s full SHA can download that spelled commit instead of its actual target.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The release archive URL uses an unqualified tag name, and archive resolution accepts object IDs and other refs, so a SHA-shaped tag name resolves the spelled commit.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when a release's tag name is the full 40-character SHA of another commit, the release's Source Code ZIP and TAR.GZ downloads contain the commit that the name spells, not the commit the tag points to.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, delete Release on an unpublished draft reports success and removes it from Releases, but its title, notes, and Draft badge stay readable at /releases/tag/<name>. The leftover record has no Git tag, isn't listed on Tags, and blocks reusing the tag name.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DeleteReleaseByID with delTag=false converts the row to IsTag rather than deleting it, even for drafts with no Git tag; draft/title/note fields and tag-name reservation survive.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, delete Release on an unpublished draft reports success and removes it from Releases, but its title, notes, and Draft badge stay readable at /releases/tag/<name>. The leftover record has no Git tag, isn't listed on Tags, and blocks reusing the tag name.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a version tag labels a point in the code history, while a release adds a title and notes for that version. Using Create Tag Only with Use the title and content of release as tag message enabled stores the entered text in the tag, but the tag page and a later New Release form show neither the title nor the notes. A comparable annotated tag created through Git displays that information correctly. The matching failure is the missing display and release prefill for the web-created tag, rather than proof that its message was never stored.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CreateNewTag creates its IsTag Release with tag/target/publisher only, passing msg only to Git tag creation. Later detail and prefill read the empty database title/note.
reproductionPaths: With "Use the title and content of release as tag message" ticked, Create Tag Only writes an annotated tag with the entered title and notes, but Gitea's tag page and the New Release prefill show neither, unlike the same annotated tag pushed with git.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, starting a release on an existing tag and saving it as a draft turns the tag's release row into a draft, and the Tags RSS/Atom feed excludes drafts, so a Git tag that still exists drops out of the feed until the release is published. The Tags page keeps such tags on purpose.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The tag feed queries release records excluding drafts; saving the existing tag as a draft changes that sole row and removes it from the feed despite the Git tag still existing.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, starting a release on an existing tag and saving it as a draft turns the tag's release row into a draft, and the Tags RSS/Atom feed excludes drafts, so a Git tag that still exists drops out of the feed until the release is published. The Tags page keeps such tags on purpose.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, at phone width on release/tag pages, the Releases/Tags tab menu can overflow onto RSS Feed, particularly with release-creation controls and multi-digit counts. The visible feed button is obscured or a tap follows Tags instead.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared releases/tags header keeps counts and action controls on a row without enough responsive width when both tab labels and counts are present.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, at phone width, for a user who can create releases, the Releases/Tags tab menu on a tag's detail page overflows onto the RSS Feed button, so the Tags tab paints over the button.

In Gitea, at phone width, for a user who can create releases, the Releases/Tags tab menu on the Releases list overflows onto the RSS Feed button once the counts have two digits, so tapping the visible RSS button opens Tags.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a successfully created long unbroken tag name does not wrap in release metadata. On the Releases list or tag detail page it widens the tag column, squeezing or pushing the release title, Edit control, metadata and downloads beyond the viewport.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Release metadata links display the entire tag name without word breaking; the flex column fixed basis cannot contain the token, pushing detail/download content beyond its intended width.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s Releases list at desktop width, a release whose valid 250-character tag name never wraps widens the tag column across the row, pushing the release title, details and Edit control out of view or squeezing them into a narrow column.

In Gitea, a successfully created 255-character slash-containing tag opens a detail page with an unwrapped name extending past the right edge, pushing downloads and tag metadata outside the desktop viewport.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, validation errors show internal field keys instead of visible field names: examples include profile Website, release Tag name/Title, branch rename, protected-tag pattern and repository Default Branch. The input can be correctly rejected while the banner says form.Website, form.TagName or a similar untranslated key.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Validate constructs form.<GoField> labels; Website has no matching translated field label and URL validation appends its internal Url message argument.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on New Release, an invalid, empty or too-long tag name shows an error that names the field with the internal key form.TagName instead of the visible 'Tag name' label.
In Gitea, saving a release with an empty title shows the error 'form.Title cannot be empty.', naming the field with its internal key instead of the visible 'Title' label.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when the New Release form is rejected by a validation error (such as an invalid or duplicate tag name), it comes back with the tag, title, notes and Pre-Release choice kept, but 'Use the title and content of release as tag message' unchecked. Correcting the tag and resubmitting then creates the tag without that message.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The add_tag_msg input has no checked binding to submitted form state, so every server-rendered error resets it.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when the New Release form is rejected by a validation error (such as an invalid or duplicate tag name), it comes back with the tag, title, notes and Pre-Release choice kept, but 'Use the title and content of release as tag message' unchecked. Correcting the tag and resubmitting then creates the tag without that message.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when New Release is opened for an existing tag (for example from the Tags page) or re-shown after a release error, changing the tag name to an unused one updates the hint to 'New tag…' but the Create Tag Only button never appears, so a tag-only creation isn't possible from that form.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ShowCreateTagOnlyButton is computed on the server; initTagNameEditor updates target/helper text but never toggles that button on name changes.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when New Release is opened for an existing tag (for example from the Tags page) or re-shown after a release error, changing the tag name to an unused one updates the hint to 'New tag…' but the Create Tag Only button never appears, so a tag-only creation isn't possible from that form.

logicalBugs.description: On Gitea’s Releases page, each release's notes are rendered separately, so two releases with the same heading text (for example '## Notes') both get the same anchor id. A link to the older release's heading lands on the newer release's heading, and the older one can't be linked from the list.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Each release note is independently passed to markdown.RenderString without a per-release heading namespace, then all results are inserted in one document.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s Releases page, each release's notes are rendered separately, so two releases with the same heading text (for example '## Notes') both get the same anchor id. A link to the older release's heading lands on the newer release's heading, and the older one can't be linked from the list.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a release title within the 255-character limit that contains CJK or emoji characters is saved shortened and ending in '…', with no error or warning. The form accepts it, but storage trims it by byte length and display width, so the user doesn't learn their title was changed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CreateRelease applies EllipsisDisplayString(title,255) after form character validation, enforcing display/byte-oriented shortening without reporting it.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, a release title within the 255-character limit that contains CJK or emoji characters is saved shortened and ending in '…', with no error or warning. The form accepts it, but storage trims it by byte length and display width, so the user doesn't learn their title was changed.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on a release's edit page, clearing an attachment's file name and clicking Update Release keeps you on the edit page because the name is required. Clicking Remove on that attachment afterwards doesn't fix it: the row is hidden while its empty name field stays required, so every later Update Release does nothing (the page doesn't move on and nothing is saved) and no message explains why, until the page is reloaded.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The remove handler hides the row and sets a deletion flag but never disables or clears required validation on its name input.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on a release's edit page, clearing an attachment's file name and clicking Update Release keeps you on the edit page because the name is required. Clicking Remove on that attachment afterwards doesn't fix it: the row is hidden while its empty name field stays required, so every later Update Release does nothing (the page doesn't move on and nothing is saved) and no message explains why, until the page is reloaded.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, creating a release with a title of only spaces passes the 'title cannot be empty' check, because the check compares against the exact empty string without trimming. The release is published with a blank, invisible heading on the Releases page. An empty title is correctly rejected.
logicalBugs.rootCause: NewReleasePost tests form.Title against the exact empty string without trimming whitespace.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, creating a release with a title of only spaces passes the 'title cannot be empty' check, because the check compares against the exact empty string without trimming. The release is published with a blank, invisible heading on the Releases page. An empty title is correctly rejected.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when editing a release, an attachment's name can be replaced with only spaces. Update Release accepts it, and the release's Downloads list then shows a row with an icon and size but no file name.
logicalBugs.rootCause: EditReleasePost copies attachment-edit fields directly into editAttachments; no trimming/nonblank validation is applied before updating attachments.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when editing a release, an attachment's name can be replaced with only spaces. Update Release accepts it, and the release's Downloads list then shows a row with an icon and size but no file name.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s standard Markdown toolbar used by wiki (repository documentation) pages and release notes, a heading button inserts # markers at the caret instead of making the current line a heading. Selecting text and changing heading levels can stack prefixes such as "# ## ### Heading" rather than replace the existing level.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared combomarkdowneditor template uses markdown-toolbar-element md-header directly. Its selection-prefix operation is not adapted to select the whole current line or normalize an existing heading prefix, so both caret insertion and repeated level changes retain incorrect Markdown.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s release notes editor, clicking a heading toolbar button (H1–H3) with the text cursor at the end of a line, and nothing selected, inserts the # marker at the cursor instead of at the start of the line, so the line doesn't become a heading. With the line selected, the button works.

In Gitea’s release notes editor, selecting text and clicking H1, then H2, then H3 adds another heading prefix each time instead of changing the level, so the text becomes '# ## ### Heading' and Preview shows a level-one heading containing literal '## ###'.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, if a release's edit form was opened before someone else saved changes, saving it (even after changing only the title) restores the older notes and pre-release setting without any warning, discarding the newer edits.
logicalBugs.rootCause: EditReleasePost assigns form Title/Content/Prerelease to the loaded release and updates it without an expected version, timestamp or original-content conflict check.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if a release's edit form was opened before someone else saved changes, saving it (even after changing only the title) restores the older notes and pre-release setting without any warning, discarding the newer edits.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, if a tag was created on a non-default branch and a release draft is then created for that existing tag, the saved draft shows the target as main instead of the tag's branch. The draft's Compare also uses main, which can wrongly say the branches are equal.
logicalBugs.rootCause: New release defaults tag_target to the repository default when the tag record has no branch target, then persists the posted target without deriving the tag ancestry/branch.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if a tag was created on a non-default branch and a release draft is then created for that existing tag, the saved draft shows the target as main instead of the tag's branch. The draft's Compare also uses main, which can wrongly say the branches are equal.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea’s EasyMDE Markdown editor used for wiki (repository documentation) pages and release notes, toolbar tooltips advertise formatting shortcuts such as "Bold (Ctrl-B)", but pressing the shortcut leaves selected text unchanged. Clicking the corresponding Bold or Italic toolbar button works.
logicalBugs.rootCause: switchToEasyMDE replaces CodeMirror extraKeys with a new map containing quick-submit and mention-navigation handlers. This discards EasyMDE formatting key bindings while its toolbar still advertises them. The Ctrl-B tooltip in the release report identifies this EasyMDE path even though that report calls it the enhanced editor; the standard textarea toolbar uses the different "Add bold text" tooltip.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea’s release notes enhanced editor, the Bold button's tooltip says "Bold (Ctrl-B)", but pressing Ctrl+B on selected text does nothing; clicking the Bold button works.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea repository's Tags page, after searching, clearing the search box and submitting, pressing the browser's Back button shows the earlier filtered results again but leaves the search box empty, so the page doesn't show what it's filtered by.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The tag search input relies on browser form restoration and has no history-state synchronization from the query URL; cached results can be restored with a later input value.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea repository's Tags page, after searching, clearing the search box and submitting, pressing the browser's Back button shows the earlier filtered results again but leaves the search box empty, so the page doesn't show what it's filtered by.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, downloading a release's source code as ZIP (or as a bundle) from the web returns a correct ZIP, but the response's Link rel="immutable" header, which tells download tools the permanent URL for the same file, points to the .tar.gz archive. Following it returns a gzip tarball instead of the ZIP.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The response Link header hardcodes .tar.gz instead of using the requested archive format.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, downloading a release's source code as ZIP (or as a bundle) from the web returns a correct ZIP, but the response's Link rel="immutable" header, which tells download tools the permanent URL for the same file, points to the .tar.gz archive. Following it returns a gzip tarball instead of the ZIP.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, draft releases are hidden from users without write access on the web (the release page returns 404 and the draft isn't listed), but a read-only collaborator can fetch the draft's title, notes and assets through the release-by-tag and release-by-id API endpoints, and download its attachments.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The single-release API retrieves the record by ID/tag and serializes it without the write-access visibility restriction used by the web draft route.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, draft releases are hidden from users without write access on the web (the release page returns 404 and the draft isn't listed), but a read-only collaborator can fetch the draft's title, notes and assets through the release-by-tag and release-by-id API endpoints, and download its attachments.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea lists published releases and version tags across numbered pages. Opening a page beyond the current last page—for example, returning to page 2 after its only release was deleted—can show a nonzero total but no items and no page-navigation controls. The list neither returns to a valid page nor lets the user reach surviving entries through its pager.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Release list queries use the requested offset without clamping to the final valid page, and the shared pager is hidden for one-page collections.
reproductionPaths: Opening a Releases (or Tags) list page number beyond the last page, for example going back to page 2 after its only release was deleted, shows the release count but no releases and no pagination controls, so there's no way from the list to reach the pages that do have releases. Gitea queries the requested page without moving it to the last page, and hides the pager when only one page exists.
